compiled_state.description:
## The defect

A gate refusal states a reason that is not a reason. Seen verbatim on a `plan_review` poll:

    "the local ticket store is 0 commit(s) BEHIND the shared store — ticket events written
     elsewhere are not in this clone's view — refusing to decide the plan-review gate against
     a ticket store that is not current"

**Zero commits behind is the definition of current.** The message asserts a staleness condition
and then reports the value that disproves it, in the same sentence, and refuses on that basis.

## Context, and why it is not merely cosmetic

Observed by an implementing agent during a plan review, alongside two OTHER refusal variants from
the same family across consecutive polls:

    "the local ticket store has DIVERGED from the shared store — neither history contains the
     other, so this clone can neither see the shared state nor publish its own"

    "the local ticket store holds 17 committed ticket event(s) the shared store has never
     received (last delivery failure: final-push-rejected)"

All three were contradicted by direct read-only inspection at the time: local `HEAD`,
`origin/tickets` and the live remote ref were all `62812ee985`, 0 ahead and 0 behind. The store is
written concurrently by eleven worktrees, so a transient snapshot mid-write is expected and the
first two messages are at least COHERENT descriptions of a state that could exist.

The third is not. It cannot be a race artefact in the same way, because the number it prints is
the one that would clear the check. Either:
- the count is computed against a different ref than the one the message names (in which case the
  message is misleading and the real comparison is unstated), or
- the boundary condition is inverted somewhere (`>= 0` where `> 0` was meant), in which case the
  gate refuses on a healthy store.

Both are worth knowing, and the second would refuse REAL work for no reason.

## Why this matters beyond one confusing string

The refusal is otherwise well-designed: it fails closed, names the condition, and says what it is
refusing to do. That is the pattern this codebase gets right and which several tickets tonight have
praised. A refusal whose stated evidence contradicts its own conclusion undermines exactly that
trust — an operator who reads it carefully has to decide whether to believe the prose or the
number, and an agent that believes the prose will retry or escalate against a healthy store.

## Not reproduced

I have NOT reproduced this deliberately. It was observed in passing and reported with the message
quoted verbatim; the contradicting measurements were taken at the same time by the observer, not by
me. First job is to make it first-hand or refute it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The refusal path is located and the `0 behind` case reproduced deterministically, or shown
      to be impossible and the observation explained another way. A refutation is a valid outcome.
- [ ] Establish which comparison actually drives the refusal and whether the message names the
      same one. If they differ, the message is corrected to name what is really compared.
- [ ] A store that is genuinely current (0 ahead, 0 behind, shared history) is never refused.
      Proven by driving the gate against such a store and observing it decide rather than refuse.
- [ ] The two sibling messages (`DIVERGED`, `N events never received`) are checked for the same
      class of mismatch between stated evidence and conclusion, and each recorded as correct or
      corrected. Do not fix only the one that was noticed.
- [ ] Whatever changes, the fail-closed posture is preserved: the fix is to stop refusing on a
      NON-reason, not to make the gate more permissive when the store really is behind.
compiled_state.title: A plan-review refusal says the store is '0 commit(s) BEHIND ... refusing to decide against a store that is not current' -- the number it prints disproves the condition it asserts
